access_links.label: Coral Reef Ecosystem Studies Project on the U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit

description: Coral Reef Ecosystem Studies Project is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange (CAKE); St. Petersburg Coastal and Marine Science Center; Dry Tortugas National Park. The Coral Reef Ecosystem Studies (CREST) project investigates the health and resilience of coral reefs to future ecosystem changes, including climate change, in the Florida Keys, U.S. Caribbean, and the Gulf. Its primary purpose is to provide data to inform public policy and best management practices for coral reef conservation and restoration. Coverage: Florida (2018). The toolkit gives Florida as the location, 2018 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
